h1: Eligibility for Udyam Registration — Who Can Apply

aiOverview.short: Eligibility for Udyam Registration depends on a business's investment in plant, machinery or equipment along with its annual turnover. Both manufacturing and service businesses can apply under the same combined criteria, with classification into micro, small or medium enterprise categories based on where these figures fall.
aiOverview.medium: Eligibility for Udyam Registration is based on two combined financial factors, the business's investment in plant, machinery or equipment, and its annual turnover. Unlike older rules that treated manufacturing and service businesses differently, both sectors are now assessed under the same combined criteria. Proprietorships, partnerships, LLPs, private limited companies and other recognised business structures can apply, provided their investment and turnover fall within the prescribed limits for micro, small or medium enterprises. Traders can also register, though certain scheme benefits may be more limited for trading businesses. Businesses exceeding the medium enterprise limits fall outside the MSME category altogether.
aiOverview.long:
Eligibility for Udyam Registration is determined by two financial factors considered together, a business's investment in plant, machinery or equipment, and its annual turnover. These two figures place a business into one of three categories, micro, small or medium enterprise, with each category having its own defined limits set by the Ministry of MSME. A key simplification introduced with Udyam is that both manufacturing and service sector businesses are evaluated under the same combined classification criteria, unlike older systems that treated them separately. Any recognised business structure, including proprietorships, partnerships, LLPs and private limited companies, engaged in manufacturing or providing services, can apply for Udyam Registration, provided their figures fall within the applicable limits. Trading businesses can also register, though they may have more limited access to certain manufacturing or service specific scheme benefits. Businesses whose investment and turnover exceed the upper limit for medium enterprises fall outside the MSME category and are not eligible for Udyam Registration.

body.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Before diving into the registration process itself, many business owners simply want to know one thing, does my business actually qualify for Udyam Registration? This page answers that question clearly, covering exactly what determines eligibility and how classification works.

body.heading: What Determines Eligibility for Udyam Registration
paragraphs: Eligibility comes down to two financial factors considered together, your investment in plant, machinery or equipment, and your annual turnover. These figures are self declared during registration and later verified against your financial records, and together they determine both your eligibility and your specific classification category.

body.heading: Business Classification — Micro, Small and Medium
paragraphs: Every eligible business falls into one of three categories, micro, small or medium enterprise, based on where their investment and turnover figures land. This classification affects which specific schemes and benefits a business can access, since some programs are targeted specifically at micro enterprises, while others extend to small or medium businesses as well.

body.heading: Who Can Apply for Udyam Registration
paragraphs: Proprietorships, partnership firms, limited liability partnerships, private limited companies, and other recognised business structures engaged in manufacturing or providing services can apply, provided their investment and turnover fall within the defined limits. This includes new startups as well as established businesses that have not previously registered.

body.heading: Business Types That Are Not Eligible
paragraphs: Businesses whose investment and turnover exceed the upper limits defined for medium enterprises fall outside the MSME category and cannot register under Udyam. Additionally, certain specific business activities may be excluded from MSME classification under government guidelines, so it is worth confirming eligibility if your business falls into a specialised sector.

body.heading: Manufacturing vs Service Businesses
paragraphs: One of the most important changes brought by Udyam Registration was unifying the classification criteria for manufacturing and service businesses. Previously, these two sectors had different investment and turnover limits, which often created confusion. Today, both are assessed under the same combined criteria, making eligibility easier to determine regardless of your business type.

body.heading: What Happens If You Grow Beyond MSME Limits
paragraphs: If your business grows and your investment or turnover increases significantly, your classification may shift from micro to small, or small to medium enterprise. Businesses that eventually exceed the upper medium enterprise limits will no longer qualify for MSME status and should update their registration status accordingly.

body.heading: How to Check Your Eligibility Before Applying
paragraphs: The simplest way to check eligibility is to compare your current investment in plant, machinery or equipment, and your most recent annual turnover, against the government's published classification limits. If you are unsure how to calculate these figures correctly, particularly what counts toward investment, it is worth getting professional guidance before applying.

paragraphs: Business owners frequently ask whether goodwill or working capital counts toward investment limits, how depreciation affects investment calculations, and whether eligibility is reassessed automatically as a business grows. These are addressed in the FAQ section.

paragraphs: Understanding eligibility for Udyam Registration comes down to knowing your investment and turnover figures accurately and comparing them against the current classification limits. Most businesses, whether manufacturing, service or trading, will find they qualify under one of the three MSME categories, making Udyam Registration accessible to the vast majority of small and growing businesses in India.
